comment: The separation between strategic governance and operational governance is useful, but the principle may be difficult to implement in small or low-capacity settings where the same body or individuals must initially perform both functions.

anchor.note: p.54 l.Lines 253-256 read as the printed page; section 3.4.2 agrees

public.text: The separation between strategic governance and operational governance is useful, but the principle may be difficult to implement in small or low-capacity settings where the same body or individuals must initially perform both functions.
public.suggestedRevision: Cross-reference Section 3.4.7 and state here that mandate and execution must be logically separated even where they are temporarily housed within one body. Require documented roles, agendas, decisions, and conflict-management procedures.
